title: Lanes by multiversioned autovectorization; the rasterizer row as a per-pixel loop
body: simd::lanes::F32s<N> (F32x4 / F32x8 / F32x16) are arrays whose operations are lane loops (index loops: core::array::from_fn and map don't always inline), and simd::Level picks the copy to run: code is compiled as the target builds it (SSE2, NEON, simd128) and on x86-64 again inside #[target_feature(enable = "avx2,fma")] and "avx512f" wrappers, detected at run time with std (cfg(target_feature) without), as Core / simd's dot kernel already did: one way of doing SIMD in the crate. No intrinsics per backend except sqrt without std (core has no f32::sqrt; each target's square-root instruction four lanes at a time, libm elsewhere). geometry::raster: RoundedRect::distance (Quilez's rounded box) and distance_lanes, coverage = saturate(0.5 - d / w), and fill_rounded_rect, premultiplied source-over into RGBA8 rows, each level byte for byte the plain loop's (tested at every level this CPU runs; one shared distance body). Measured, 1920 x 1080 frame, results identical: 3.5x a plain per-pixel loop at the SSE2 baseline, 6.7x with AVX2, 9.0-9.9x with AVX-512. Not done from the intent: Core / simd's dot kernel moving onto the lanes, and vector square roots in the row kernel without std (libm per pixel there, so wasm and other no-std builds run it scalar): both a todo.

title: A row kernel over sixteen-lane groups stayed scalar
body: The first fill_rounded_rect processed the row in F32s<16> groups (distance, coverage, blend per group): 1.4-1.9x a plain loop, AVX-512 no faster than AVX2. Reading the assembly: core::array::try_from_fn called out of line (from_fn and map behind a drop guard don't always inline); after replacing them with index loops, the group loop's body still had sixteen vsqrtss per iteration (the SLP vectorizer left the straight-line group scalar once its results fed per-lane integer packing), while the remainder path got vsqrtps zmm. Also costly: saturating float-to-u8/u32 casts and u32-to-f32 conversions, which have no vector instruction before AVX-512. Rewriting the row as a per-pixel loop for the loop vectorizer (a 32-bit index to float, pixels as words split by shifts, clamp then to_int_unchecked) gave 3.5x / 6.7x / 9.9x. Lessons: read the assembly before tuning (count ss against ps ops and look for calls), write whole-array kernels as per-element loops and let the loop vectorizer pick the width, avoid saturating and unsigned float/int conversions in vector code, and never use f32::clamp before to_int_unchecked (it keeps NaN; max then min doesn't).

title: Core / simd's dot kernel onto the lanes, and vector sqrt without std
body: Two pieces of the simd lanes intent left: (1) simd::dot_kernel (Fir, Resampler, the Signal reductions) dispatched through simd::Level like the rasterizer, with an AVX-512 copy, measured against today's kernel and NumPy before switching (bench/numpy rows that use dot). (2) The rasterizer's square root without std: f32::sqrt is std-only, so the row kernel calls libm per pixel in no-std builds (parda's wasm build): a per-target sqrt the loop vectorizer can widen (or the row in four-lane chunks with each target's instruction), measured on wasm32 with simd128 under wasmtime.
